fields.title: Nothing checks that an alert names an owner and a first action

sections.What it checks:
* [std-OBS.somebody-acts-on-every-alert] says an alert "**MUST** name the accountable owner and the first action to
  take".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The check this rule needs is a pipeline job over the alert rule files. It lists every rule with an
`alert:` key whose `owner` label or `first_action` annotation is empty:

```sh
yq '.groups[].rules[] | select(has("alert"))
    | select((.labels.owner // "") == "" or (.annotations.first_action // "") == "") | .alert' alerts/*.yaml
```

The job fails where that prints a name. It fails as well where either value is a placeholder: `TODO`, `TBD`, `FIXME`
or a value in angle brackets. The same query can run as a pre-commit check, or as a Claude Code hook on `Write` and
`Edit`.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the alert rules is the only thing that notices a missing owner today.

The standard names no field for the owner or the first action, so the check assumes `owner` and `first_action`. It proves a value is present, and a reviewer still judges whether the first action is one somebody can take. The other rules under [std-OBS.somebody-acts-on-every-alert] go unchecked, and so does [std-OBS.one-request-reads-as-one-timeline].
